--- order: 2 unit: parts title: "Navbar, cards and a grid" summary: "Rebuild the club page's menu, cards and form with Bootstrap: each part is a fixed shape of nested tags with class names, and the grid's row and col line the cards up." language: html introduces: [bs-component, bs-grid] voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-html" 8130 url: http://127.0.0.1:8130/index.html ready: HTML code layout: full pacing: keyDelayMs: 18 explainPicture: page.html#explain explainClip: query: { code: "@page.html#explain-start", zoom: 1.5 } caption: "A row holds cols; each col shares the width; a card goes inside a col" clip: - caption: "A row is Bootstrap's line of columns. It is empty." - wait: 1200 - caption: "A col inside it, and a card inside the col: the shape from the cards." - type: { into: HTML code, text: "
\n
Beginners

\n", after: "
\n" } - caption: "One col takes the whole row." - wait: 600 - caption: "A second col, and the two share the row equally." - type: { into: HTML code, text: "
\n
Players
\n
\n", after: "Beginners
\n \n" } - expect: { selector: "#preview-text", contains: "Players" } - caption: "No Flexbox rules of your own. Row and col did the layout." - wait: 1200 hook: "A navbar, a row of cards and a sign-up form: most websites you visit are built from these same few parts." --- In the club page you built the menu, the cards and the form from tags and your own CSS. Bootstrap has each of them ready-made. A Bootstrap part is a **shape**: tags nested in a fixed way, each with its class name. Copy the shape, then change the words. The cards sit in Bootstrap's **grid**: a `row` holds `col`s, and the cols share the row's width. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#predict insight: "The grid is the part a wrong guess is likely on; seeing equal columns appear from class names alone sets up the idea of copying a shape." check: type: predict q: "How will the three cards be placed?" options: - "Side by side, sharing the width equally" - "One under another, each the full width" - "Side by side, each only as wide as its word" - "On top of each other, in the same place" actual: "Side by side, sharing the width equally. The row lines up what is inside it, and each col takes an equal share, so three cols take a third each." ``` `row` and `col` are new. Each card sits inside a `col`, and the cols sit inside a `row`. ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#run try: { playground: html, starter: "page.html#run", height: 460 } insight: "Each part is a shape of nested tags: navbar > container > brand and nav links; row > col > card > card-body." check: { type: reflect, text: "I can find the navbar, a row, a col and a card in the code." } unlocks: [navbar, card, row-and-col] ``` Compare with your prediction. Switch on **Boxes** to see the shapes nest. Then delete one whole `col` (from `
` to its closing `
`) and watch the other two share the row. ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#run picture: page.html#run insight: "Bootstrap's parts are fixed shapes with fixed names, and they replace the CSS students wrote by hand." tasks: - check: type: match q: "Match each class with its job in the shape." pairs: - ["navbar", "the bar across the top"] - ["navbar-brand", "the club's name, on the left of the bar"] - ["nav-link", "one link in the menu"] - ["row", "holds cols in a line"] - ["col", "one equal share of the row"] - ["card-body", "the padding inside a card"] explain: "The nesting matters: a col goes straight inside a row, a card-body straight inside a card. Copy the whole shape from the Reference card." - check: type: number q: "Your hand-built club page needed about 40 lines of CSS for its header, menu and cards. How many lines of CSS of its own does this page have?" answer: 0 explain: "None. The CSS is in bootstrap.min.css. That is the trade: no rules to write, but class names to look up, and a page that looks like many other Bootstrap pages." - check: type: bug code: page.html#bug text: "Beginners fills the whole width, and the other two cards sit on a line underneath. There is no error. Click the line that is wrong." answer: 5 fault: logic misconception: bs-made-up-class explain: "Bootstrap has no class called column, so the browser ignores it and that box takes the whole row. The name is col." ``` ### Name the parts Each class has a job. ### Count the CSS Compare with your club page. ### Spot the bug One card is too wide. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "Adding a part is copying its shape into the right place." try: { playground: html, starter: "page.html#run", height: 460 } tasks: - hint: - "A button in a card goes inside its card-body, after the text." - "A link can look like a button: a class=\"btn btn-primary\" with href=\"#join\". Put one in each card-body." expected: page.html#sol-buttons check: { type: code, text: "Put a Join button in each card.", rules: { contains: ["btn btn-"] } } - hint: - "Bootstrap styles a form when each part has its class: form-label, form-control, form-select." - "Add a container with id=\"join\" under the cards: a heading, a label and box for the name, a select for the group, and a button. Look up form-control on the Reference cards." expected: page.html#sol-form check: { type: code, text: "Add a sign-up form under the cards, with Bootstrap's form classes.", rules: { contains: ["form-label", "form-control"] } } unlocks: [form-control] ``` ### A button in each card Inside the card's body. ### A sign-up form Labels and boxes with Bootstrap's form classes. ## Make: results and a footer ```step stage: make insight: "Looking up a part students have not used before and fitting it into the page is the everyday Bootstrap skill." try: { playground: html, starter: "page.html#make", height: 420 } check: { type: code, text: "Add a Bootstrap table of results and a footer.", rules: { contains: ["class=\"table", " Read the unit primer first. Each Bootstrap component is a **shape**: tags nested in a fixed order, each with its class (`navbar` > `container` > `navbar-brand` and `navbar-nav`; `row` > `col` > `card` > `card-body`). Students do not invent these; they copy the shape from the Reference card or getbootstrap.com and change the words. The **grid**: a `row` lines up its `col`s and shares the width equally (it is Flexbox inside, the same idea as their hand-built `.cards { display: flex; }`). The navbar uses `navbar-expand`, so it never folds into a menu button: folding needs Bootstrap's JavaScript, which this course leaves out. The planted bug is a made-up class name (`column`): the browser ignores names it has no rule for, silently. This is the most common Bootstrap slip. running: - "Predict: ask students to say what row and col might each do before running." - "Run: switch on Boxes and trace the nesting with a finger: row, col, card, card-body." - "Investigate: put a hand-built club page on the board for the count-the-CSS question." - "Modify: for the form, the Reference card has the shape; students add the classes to tags they already know." - 'Make: the table class is new. Ask "where would you look it up?" rather than giving it.' struggle: Students guess class names (column, blue, big-button) and expect them to work. Ask "is that name on the Reference card?" every time, rather than correcting it for them. stuck: - see: A card fills the whole width while the others share a line. ask: Is its box's class exactly col? fix: Use col, not column or cols; only Bootstrap's own names do anything. - see: Cards stack one under another. ask: Are the cols inside one row? fix: Put every col straight inside the same div with class row. - see: Text touches the card's border. ask: Is there a card-body inside the card? fix: Wrap the card's content in div class="card-body". stretch: Give the cards different widths with col-8 and col-4 (a row is 12 parts), or add a badge to a card title. Try an image across the top of a card with card-img-top. support: Give students the card shape on paper with blanks for the class names. leads: "Next lesson: your own CSS on top of Bootstrap, and when writing CSS by hand is the better choice. Class idea: hold up the hand-built club page and this one and ask which was quicker, and which is more theirs." exit: q: What goes inside a row, and what goes inside a col? a: Cols go inside a row and share its width; the content, such as a card, goes inside a col. explain: > 1. A `row` is a line of columns. 2. Put a `col` inside it, and a `card` inside the col: one col takes the whole row. 3. Add a second col: the two share the row equally. 4. No Flexbox rules of your own: Bootstrap's `row` and `col` do the layout. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-buttons step-4#t2: page.html#sol-form step-5: page.html#sol-make sources: - title: "Bootstrap 5.3: Grid system" url: https://getbootstrap.com/docs/5.3/layout/grid/ checked: 2026-10-12 - title: "Bootstrap 5.3: Navbar" url: https://getbootstrap.com/docs/5.3/components/navbar/ checked: 2026-10-12 ```
